aboutH2: Milestone House: Men's Sober Living in NDG, Montreal
intro: Milestone House is built on the idea that recovery becomes stronger when people can practice it in everyday life. It is a men’s sober living home that supports individuals working through addiction to alcohol, drugs, prescription medications, and various process addictions like gambling, excessive gaming, or technology dependence. The program is structured around community living, phased progress, daily routines, and steady involvement in the 12 Step approach. Residents have access to a supportive sober environment where they can rebuild stability, develop accountability, and grow their confidence as they move toward long term independence.

pillars.title: Building Lasting Recovery Through Consistent Daily Action
pillars.body: The Milestone House model focuses on community connection and consistent daily action. Residents participate in 12 Step activities, receive guidance from peers who are further along in their recovery, and follow a clear structure that helps strengthen healthy habits. Regular meetings, step work, and meaningful peer relationships all play a role in reinforcing sobriety. Group fitness, shared routines, and responsibilities throughout the home help individuals build emotional resilience, practice better decision making, and experience a stable environment that encourages steady growth.

pillars.title: A Home Environment Built for Focus, Balance, and Growth
pillars.body: Residents stay in a bright and modern home that has been designed to support routine and purpose. Comfortable living areas, shared spaces for connection, and a private on site gym create a setting where daily structure feels natural. Communal meals, household tasks, and regular check ins offer consistency while giving residents the chance to practice real life skills in a safe and supportive way. The location in NDG provides convenient access to the city, offering opportunities to put recovery principles into practice throughout the day and return to a stable and welcoming home each night.

pillars.title: Started by a Montrealer Who Went Through It Himself
pillars.body: Milestone House was founded by Matthew Torralbo, who grew up in Montreal and is a certified CCAR Recovery Coach. His own recovery took him to Ethos Recovery's sober living community in Los Angeles, where he later worked as a house manager, and he brought that community model home to NDG. He now runs Milestone House as founder and house manager. A staff member lives in the house around the clock, and men who are further along in recovery mentor the newer residents.

overview: Milestone House is a sober living home, and its website says plainly that it is not a clinical program. It lists no doctors, nurses or therapists on staff, and it does not offer detox. What the house provides is structure: live-in staff, daily check-ins, daily AA, NA or CA meetings, step work with a sponsor, random drug testing and house rules that relax as residents earn more responsibility. For therapy, the house refers residents to outpatient clinics and therapists it has relationships with.

afterOverview: Most men arrive after finishing rehab, though the house says it is open to men at any stage. Because there is no detox, anyone who still needs withdrawal management has to arrange it elsewhere first. The first three months are core programming inside the house. After that, residents can go back to work or school while they keep living there, and many stay for up to a year. Recovery.com lists Milestone House as private pay, and the house does not publish its fees.

location.heading: Milestone House in Montreal, Quebec
location.intro: The house is at 5275 Avenue Beaconsfield in Notre-Dame-de-Grâce (NDG), on the Island of Montreal, a few minutes from the cafés and shops of Monkland Village. Downtown Montreal and Westmount are about 15 minutes away by car, Laval and Longueuil on the South Shore take roughly 25 to 30 minutes, and Ottawa is about two hours west.

faqIntro: Answers come from Milestone House's own website, its listing and recovery.com. Still unsure? Call, it's free and confidential.

faqs.q: Is Milestone House a rehab or a sober living home?
faqs.a: It is a sober living home for men, not a treatment centre. The house describes itself as a community-based model rather than a clinical program, so there is no detox, medical care or in-house therapy. Residents get structure, live-in staff, 12-step work and peer support, and the house refers them to outpatient therapists when needed.

faqs.q: How much does Milestone House cost?
faqs.a: Milestone House does not publish its fees. Recovery.com lists it as private pay and has no pricing for it either. Call 514-865-1334 or email info@milestone.house to ask about cost, what is included and availability.
The minimum stay is three months. Beyond that, length of stay depends on each person’s needs, and many choose to stay up to a year, until they feel confident living independently.

No. The house says it does not offer detox services. If you still need medically supervised withdrawal, arrange that first through a detox program or your local CIUSSS, then ask Milestone House about moving in.

faqs.q: Who can live at Milestone House?
faqs.a: The program is open to men, including young adults, who are committed to staying substance free and following a structured recovery routine.

It is at 5275 Avenue Beaconsfield in NDG (Notre-Dame-de-Grâce), Montreal, H3X 3R9, a few minutes from Monkland Village. The house points to good public transit links nearby, and downtown Montreal is about 15 minutes by car.

faqs.q: Is there staff in the house around the clock?
faqs.a: Yes. A dedicated staff member lives on site 24/7, and staff check in with residents every day. Founder Matthew Torralbo, a certified CCAR Recovery Coach, is also the house manager.

faqs.q: Can I work or go to school while living there?
faqs.a: Yes, once the first three months are done. Those months are core programming in the house. After that, residents can start working or studying while they keep living at Milestone House and following its routine.

Yes. Families get regular updates, and the house says its team works with families throughout a resident's stay with support and guidance. Family therapy is not offered in the house, but staff can refer you to outside therapists.

faqs.q: Is Milestone House English or French speaking?
faqs.a: The house's website is in English only, and recovery.com lists English as its language. French is not mentioned, so ask when you call if you would rather speak French.
Milestone House is a men’s sober living home that provides structure, support, and a safe environment for people in recovery.

faqs.q: What kind of support do residents receive?
faqs.a: Residents benefit from daily routines, peer support, 12 Step involvement, skill building, and an environment that encourages healthy habits.

faqs.q: What are the living conditions like?
faqs.a: The home is clean, modern, and supportive, offering shared or private rooms, community spaces, and clear house rules that help maintain a safe recovery focused setting.
